AI catastrophe model · methodology

How AI-related losses arise

Expand a branch to see the question it asks and why its answers need different estimates; open a terminal category for its precise scope and forecasting status.

Each admitted incident, with all its losses, belongs to one terminal category, so incident counts and losses add within every branch. Incidents below the one admission threshold are an unestimated leftover.

Filters are overlapping navigation aids, not partitions or totals. Harm labels describe whole scenario populations, cross-sector categories appear under every sector, and intervention labels name possible control points, not measured effects.

    What the labels mean

    Separate forecast
    One scenario forecasts one terminal population.
    Shared forecast
    One scenario forecasts several terminal populations together, once. No separate estimates or weights are implied.
    Unestimated
    No scenario estimates this population. It is unquantified, not zero.
    Unsupported
    The history has no named origin, so no scenario can estimate it. It is unquantified, not zero.

    A scenario's modeled severity scope can exclude some components of the incidents in its category; open the scope to see them.

    “Other” categories hold in-scope histories that fit no named answer; they do not absorb harm outside the model's monetary loss measure.
